title: 'He didn't deserve to die': Man who died in police custody was just protecting his bike, says friend
article: A pal of Ben Matson, who died in police custody last week, said he was just trying to protect his Harley-Davidson from someone who claimed to be a Mountie.
"I don't want Ben to be made out to be some wild-eyed guy who went crazy on the street and people saying, 'Good, there's one less crazy on the street,'" Cord Copeland, 40, told The Province.

"It's just a tragic event, and I didn't want everyone to think he was some kind of a maniac. People were stealing his motorcycle, or so he thought. He was just protecting his bike like anyone would protect . . . any of their property."
Matson, 49, of Burnaby, was arrested early last Sunday and died soon after.

Police said they responded to a report of a man with a knife in the 600-block Davie at about 2:20 a.m. They said Matson was arrested after a brief chase, and went into cardiac arrest when he was subdued. He was rushed to hospital and died shortly after.
Police spokesman Scott Driemel said the officers used only physical force to subdue Matson. He did not know if Matson had a knife.
Const. Sarah Bloor said preliminary results show Matson died by choking on his own vomit. An internal police inquiry into the death is underway.
Copeland, a Vancouver City waterworks employee, said Matson joined him and his buddies at the Yale Hotel's blues bar at about 1 a.m. He had parked his yellow low-rider Harley on the street outside.
"He might have had a beer," said Copeland. "He didn't seem drunk or stoned or flipped out."
When someone saw four men moving his motorcycle, Matson raced out and confronted them. Copeland followed.
"I didn't see one, but police say he had a knife, a buck knife, that he was waving at the four men," said Copeland.
Copeland said one of the men reached into a pouch, and Matson asked him if he had a gun.
"But he pulled out an RCMP badge in one hand and had a cellphone in the other and he said he was calling the police," Copeland said.
The men said they were moving the motorcycle because it had boxed in their car. Copeland said he and Matson returned to the bar and the four men left.
A short time later, Copeland said, four male Vancouver police officers with guns drawn and one female officer with a Taser stun gun rushed into the pub past Copeland. Matson bolted out the back door.
"I don't know why he sprinted out the door," said Copeland. "I think he panicked."
It wasn't until the next day that Copeland realized it was Matson who had died. "He didn't deserve to die. He didn't do anything wrong.
"The guy who identified himself as a police officer, he left, he never stuck around to explain what happened. That guy there is who I hold 100-per-cent responsible for what happened."
RCMP spokesman Sgt. Grant Learned said it would be "totally inappropriate" to comment on an incident under investigation by Vancouver police.
